newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts satisfied with Desc Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Analysts satisfied with Desc Q1 earnings.

text.p: Analysts were generally pleased with overall earnings posted by Mexican conglomerate Desc Sociedad de Fomento Industrial (Desc), but expressed misgivings about weaknesses in some of the company's divisions.
Desc on Friday posted net earnings of 444.9 million pesos, or 1.48 pesos per share, compared with an average of 1.41 pesos predicted by four analysts previously surveyed by Reuters.
Consolidated net sales for the group were up 3.2 percent in real terms to 3.326 billion pesos for the first quarter.
Sales grew strongly in the autoparts and agribusiness divisions, but were down in the chemicals, consumer products and real estate divisions.
"Autoparts and Chemicals, the main cash-flow drivers, were pretty much as expected," said Shayne McGuire of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico.
"My attention was drawn by the strength of the export-led sectors in a tough peso environment," said Daniel Goldstein, an analyst with ING-Barings in Mexico City.
Desc's autoparts division accounted for 41.6 percent of the group's total sales, and were up 20.7 percent in real terms to 1.328 billion pesos for the first quarter.
A Desc news release said this increase was mainly due to "significant growth in autoparts, the domestic auto market recovery and the inclusion of sales by Borg-Warner."
Borg-Warner Automotive Inc sold a U.S.-based transmission plant in October 1996 to Transmisiones y Equipos Mecanicos, S.A. de C.V., a joint venture between Desc and Dana Corp.
Desc said results from the transmission plant were incorporated into group results as from January 1, 1997.

Goldstein said the incorporation increased sales but reduced margins due to the process of relocating the plant to the Mexican city of Queretaro, 200 kilometres northwest of Mexico City. Nonetheless, he estimated relocation would no longer eat into margins as of the beginning of 1998.

Kerry McHugh, of Goldman Sachs in New York, was less impressed with the autoparts division. "Autoparts exports looked soft," she wrote in a report on Friday, adding that total sales for the division were 5 percent short of her original estimates.

The chemicals division accounted for 35.2 percent of the group's total sales. Sales in this division totalled 1.170 billion pesos in the first quarter, but were down 18.2 percent in real year-on-year terms.
"We don't really understand the apparent weakness in chemical sales," McHugh said, "and will wait see what management says in their conference call on Monday."

Desc's third-biggest division, agribusiness, accounted for 18.2 percent of total sales. Agribusiness sales for the first quarter were 604.6 million pesos, up a real 43.5 percent from the year-ago quarter.
"Agribusiness had a terrific quarter... The question is, is this sustainable," McHugh wrote.
The two remaining divisions, consumer products and real estate, both posted real year-on-year reductions in sales.

McGuire said slack demand for adhesives used in the urban construction industry and disappointing real estate earnings showed a sluggish turnaround in the domestic economy, although they were minor disappointments for the group as a whole.
"It is clear there is not much recovery in the domestic economy," he said. "These are two areas in which you would expect demand if a recovery were under way."
